question.prompt: Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle. The measures of the non-overlapping minor arcs \(AB,\) \(BC,\) and \(CA\) are, respectively, \(x+75^\circ,\) \(2x+25^\circ,\) \(3x-22^\circ.\) Then one interior angle of the triangle, in degrees, is:

solutions.explanation:
The three non-overlapping arcs go around the circle once, so their measures sum to \(360^\circ\):
\[
(x+75^\circ)+(2x+25^\circ)+(3x-22^\circ)=360^\circ.
\]
Combining terms gives \(6x+78^\circ=360^\circ\), hence \(x=47^\circ\). The arc measures are therefore
\[
\widehat{AB}=122^\circ,\qquad
\widehat{BC}=119^\circ,\qquad
\widehat{CA}=119^\circ.
\]
Each is positive and less than \(180^\circ\), as required for the stated minor arcs. The inscribed angle \(\angle ACB\) intercepts arc \(AB\), so the inscribed angle theorem gives
\[
\angle ACB=\frac12(122^\circ)=61^\circ.
\]
Thus one interior angle is \(61^\circ\), choice D.
solutions.title: Find the arcs, then halve the intercepted arc
